expectations.name: 01-page-written
expectations.text: A decision record is written under docs/adrs/, the kind the map gives a foundation decision such as the job queue.

expectations.name: 02-structure
expectations.text:
Each page the agent wrote or changed meets the map's structural rules: a declared kind, listed in its guide, links
and anchors that resolve, the kind's sections in order, a record named NNNN-<slug>.md, no rejected synonym.

expectations.name: 03-lead
expectations.text: The record opens with a lead under its title, not a restatement of the title.

expectations.name: 04-reason-told
expectations.text:
The record's Context tells what happened, the incident with Redis evicting queued jobs and what it cost, before it
states a conclusion such as "we need a durable queue".
expectations.evidence: Context opens with the incident: "Redis ran out of memory and evicted keys, including queued receipt jobs. No error was logged. By March 4, 300 members had paid without receiving a receipt... Nadia resent the receipts by hand from the orders table, which took most of her Tuesday." It then notes "Redis served only the job queue, and Tom was the only volunteer who knew how to restore it" and names the forces ("prevent another loss of queued work, avoid leaving recovery dependent on one volunteer, and keep a pantry order and its queued job together"). Context states no conclusion; the choice appears only under Options and Decision.

expectations.name: 05-fact-stated
expectations.text: The record's Decision names procrastinate, the product chosen.
expectations.evidence: match /## Decision\s.*procrastinate/ in ['docs/adrs/0002-keep-background-jobs-in-postgres.md']: {'docs/adrs/0002-keep-background-jobs-in-postgres.md': '## Decision\n\nKeep background jobs in Postgres using procrastinate, replacing Celery and its Redis queue. Enqueue a job i'}
